references.text: The same formulation that the Israelites did what was evil in the Lord's sight and served the Baals and the Asherah images. This is the first occurrence of this formula in Judges.
Repetition of the formula that the Israelites did what was evil in the Lord's sight, which introduces the next cycle of oppression.
The same pattern repeats: The Israelites again did what was evil in the Lord's sight.
Once more the Israelites did what was evil in the Lord's sight, leading to the oppression by the Midianites.
A detailed description of idolatry that includes the Baals, the same theme as in 3:7.
The Asherah poles (Asherim) are mentioned alongside idolatry, the same goddesses as in Judges 3:7.
A warning against forgetting the Lord who brought them out of Egypt, exactly what Israel did in Judges 3:7.
A warning about the consequences of forgetting the Lord and following other gods.
The Israelites did what was evil in the Lord's sight and set up Asherah poles.
The worship of Baal and Asherah under Ahab, the same idols mentioned in Judges 3:7.
The prophet Jeremiah accuses the people of having followed Baal and forgotten the Lord.
